contexts.text: Without a knowledge and acknowledgement of these in himself he cannot be reformed.
As long as he is living in the world he continues in a state of reformation and regeneration.
An end, namely, of reformation and regeneration.
Unless a man is reformed and regenerated, he not only remains as he was born, but becomes even worse.
The Reformation of the Church. Signification, Explanation.
Evil Spirits are left with man, that they may excite his cupidities... so that they can be bent by the Lord into good, and the man thus be reformed.
In the spiritual man, reformation begins from the earth, or external man; but in the celestial, from the internal man, or heaven.
As this man had to be reformed as to the understanding, before he could be reformed as to the will... AC 645. AC 652.
When he thinks and acts from charity, he is reformed or regenerated, not before.
As they could be reformed. Signified, Explained... As to the reformations of the nations...
Without proprium acquired through freedom... no man can ever be reformed, because he cannot receive a new will...
Without this freedom... man can never be reformed, and receive any heavenly proprium. AC 2876.
That man may be reformed, and thus regenerated, which is effected through Knowledges and scientifics...
A potter = reformation and regeneration.
Before man comes into this (first state of the Church) he must be reformed, which is effected by certain species of temptation...
The entire process of the reformation and regeneration of those who are becoming men of the Church here represented by Lot. Treated of.
Those who are becoming spiritual, from the first state of their reformation to the last. Treated of. AC 2678. AC 2679. AC 2682:2.
Those who cannot be reformed, described.
Who can be kept... in the affection of good and truth, and thus be reformed and become spiritual, and who cannot. Explained.
The state of desolation of those who are being reformed and becoming spiritual. Treated of.
For at this day few are reformed. Those who can be reformed, if not here, yet in the other life, are brought into this state... called vastation, or desolation. AC 2694:end, Explained.
Wilderness is predicated both of those who are afterwards reformed, and of those who cannot be reformed. Illustrated.
No one can come into heavenly freedom, except through reformation by the Lord.
For man, in order to be reformed, must think truth as of himself, and do good as of himself; (otherwise) there is never any reformation or regeneration.
In the Spiritual Church... man is reformed by the Lord as to the intellectual part...
They wanted to... reform themselves. Signified. AC 2960.

The first state of all who are being reformed and made spiritual (is) that they do not believe that they are reformed by the Lord, but by themselves; that is, that everything of the will of good and of the thought of truth is from themselves; and they are left in this state by the Lord, because otherwise they cannot be reformed. Explained.
The redemption, or reformation and Salvation of the men of the Spiritual Church, is effected through truth; but that of the men of the Celestial Church through good. Explained.
In their third state, they believe that they are reformed by the Lord. Explained.
The man of the Church is reformed, that is, the truth of faith is implanted in him, and this is conjoined with the good of charity.
All being reformed and regenerated, are gifted by the Lord with charity and faith, but everyone according to his faculty... AC 2967:2, Illustrated.
For man is reformed as to both (the will and the understanding). Explained.
When man is being reformed, the general things in the natural man are disposed by the Lord to correspondence with the things which are in Heaven...
Exploration is with every man who is being reformed. Explained.
That he who is reformed has need only to be cleansed as to natural things... and then all things are disposed into order by the influx of spiritual things. Signified.
When man is being reformed, he (accounts it a duty) to hate no one.

The faculty that he can understand what is good and true although he does not will it, is given to man that he may be reformed and regenerated... But with the evil there is no affection of truth for the sake of life... and therefore they cannot be reformed; whereas with the good there is (this affection), and therefore they can be reformed. But the first state of the reformation of these is that truth... appears to be in the first place...
(Thus) an image of man's reformation is presented in his formation in the womb.
When reformation is accomplished by the ministry of truth...
By compulsion man cannot be reformed. Explained.
When man is in good, such good as serves for the reformation of his life inflows through the Societies.

For all being reformed suppose at first that good is from themselves, and thus that by the good they do they merit salvation... But those who suffer themselves to be regenerated do not confirm this... For, so long as one is in the external man, as all are in the beginning of reformation, he cannot but think so...
Unless man could receive truths (before good) he could not be reformed.
Man, when being reformed, first learns truths... and stores them up in the memory. He who cannot be reformed believes... that this is sufficient...

Every man must be reformed... In order to be regenerated, he must first be reformed, and this through the truths of faith. He learns them from the Word... This is the first state, and is called the state of reformation. Most are introduced into this state... but still few are regenerated...
With the man who is being reformed, general truths are first insinuated, then particulars, ... and finally singulars.
If when man does not receive (the inflowing good) he feels anxiety... there is hope that he can be reformed; (otherwise) the hope vanishes.
What is successive of reformation. Signified, Explained.
Therefore, as to their interiors, (the Israelites) could not be reformed.
With those being reformed (such nuclei in the skull) are reduced to softness. Explained.
If (Providence acted openly) man could never be reformed.
The Lord's making clay of spittle, etc. represented the reformation of man, who is born in ignorance of truth, and that reformation is effected through the good of faith.

When man is being reformed, he is kept as to his internal man in good and truth; and as to the external is let into his evils and falsities... but there must then be good and truth in the external in which the influx from the internal can be fixed; thus good can be among the evils and falsities, and yet be safe. Into this state is let every man who is being reformed...

For while man lives (here) he is continually kept in the state that he can be reformed, provided that, from freedom, he desists from evils; whereas, after death... he who is in evil can no longer be reformed...
For even evil men have Angels with them, in order that they can, if they will, ... be reformed.
When man is being reformed, he is kept in equilibrium... When, therefore, man has been so far reformed that he wills good, and is affected with it, then good removes evil...
In the world, however, man can think, and even understand, otherwise than he wills; but this is in order that he can be reformed...
He who does good solely from obedience... can indeed be reformed, but not regenerated. The reformation of such is here treated of.

Those who from infancy have thought little about eternal life... but have lived a good moral life... when they come to more adult age, cannot be reformed otherwise than by the adjunction of spiritual good when they are in combat...

Those in truths and not in the corresponding good... cannot be regenerated, but only reformed. For to be regenerated is said of those who through truths of faith suffer themselves to be brought to the good of spiritual life; whereas to be reformed is said of those who through truths of faith suffer themselves to be brought... only to the delight of natural life. Those who suffer themselves to be regenerated, act from affection according to the precepts of faith; whereas those who suffer themselves... to be only reformed, act not from affection, but from obedience. Explained.
Unless there were adjoined to man Spirits such as he is... he could not be withdrawn from his evils, and be reformed.
But with those who cannot be reformed and regenerated, good Spirits are also adjoined... but their immediate conjunction is with evil Spirits...
For, after death, man can no longer be reformed by instruction. Explained.
These (Genii) are warded off from every man concerning whom there is any hope of reformation.
The reason man cannot be reformed unless he has freedom. Explained. LJ 33.
When man is thinking what is good and true, in proportion, then, as he does not love evil and falsity, the Lord implants the former in his love and will, thus in his life, and so reforms him.
Man can be held in good in so far as he is being reformed.
That the Lord is called the Son of Man where it treats of reformation, etc. Illustrated.
Every word there describes... the Divine power of reforming the gentiles.

Through the capability of the understanding to be elevated into Heaven without the will, it is that man can be reformed and become spiritual; but he is then first reformed and made spiritual when his will also is elevated.

The means of reformation which the Lord has provided are these: that man is born in mere ignorance; that one newly born is kept in a state of external innocence, then in a state of external charity, and then in a state of external friendship...
The first state is called reformation; the second, regeneration. Explained.

Such is the change of state called reformation and regeneration. The state of the natural mind before reformation, may be compared to a spiral twisting downwards; but after reformation to one twisting upwards; and therefore before reformation, man looks downwards to Hell; but after reformation, upwards to Heaven.
Therefore man... is reformed and regenerated in freedom.
Man's first state, of damnation; his second state, of reformation; and his third state, of regeneration: their quality.
Man's state of reformation is when he begins to think about Heaven from the joy there... Explained.

That no one is reformed through miracles and signs. General article. (Nor though visions and speaking with the dead. DP 134, Explained.) (Nor through threats and penalties. DP 136, Explained.) (Nor in states of non-rationality and non-freedom. DP 138, Explained.) (Nor in a state of fear. DP 139, Explained.) (Nor in a state of misfortune. DP 140, Explained.) (Nor in a state of mental disorder. DP 141, Explained.) (Nor in a state of bodily disease. DP 142, Explained.) (Nor in a state of ignorance. DP 143, Explained.) (Nor in a state of blindness of the understanding. DP 144, Explained.)
If they desire truths from the affection of them, they are reformed in the Spiritual World after death.
That the external man is to be reformed through the internal, and not contrariwise. General article.
How the internal man is reformed, and through it the external. The internal man is not reformed by merely knowing, understanding, and being wise... but by willing...

When man (knowing these things) does not will evil because it is from Hell, but wills good because it is from Heaven, he is in the first degree of reformation... When he wills to desist from evils, he is in the second degree of reformation, and is then out of Hell, but not yet in Heaven. There must be this internal for man to be reformed; but unless both the external and the internal are reformed, the man is not reformed. The external is reformed through the internal, when the external desists from evils, which the internal does not will because they are infernal, and still more when it shuns them, and fights against them. Illustrated.
These can be reformed; the former cannot.
Man (would then) recede from the way of reformation, and perish.
That man may be let into the wisdom of spiritual things and also into the love of them, and still not be reformed. Explained.
Those let into spiritual love are reformed; but those let only into natural love are not reformed.

The Lord is in the interiors of man after reformation; but the devil, before it. In proportion, therefore, as man suffers himself to be reformed, the devil is cast out; but in in proportion as he does not suffer himself to be reformed, the devil remains.
The understanding, from the truths in the memory... must teach... the man what to do: this is the principal means of reformation.
He who thinks against God is rarely punished (here), because here man is always in a state of reformation; but he is punished in the Spiritual World... for then he can no longer be reformed.
Everyone, in every heresy... can be reformed...
That every man is in evil, and that he must be withdrawn from evil that he may be reformed. Explained.

a. Death is a continuation of life, with the difference that man cannot then be reformed. All reformation is effected in what is full, that is, in primes and ultimates simultaneously, and ultimates... are reformed (here), and cannot be afterwards, because... they are then quiescent... DP 307:2.

All the laws of the Divine Providence have for their end the reformation, and thus the Salvation, of man; thus the inversion of his state (from) infernal to heavenly; which can only be done progressively...

(Thus) all these things, in the order in which they are, must be repaired and converted by the Lord, in order that man may be reformed; and this can only be done... successively, from man's first age to his last.
All reformation is effected through truth, Explained.
That every man can be reformed. Chapter.
To him that overcometh = him who is fighting against his evils and falsities, and is being reformed.
That he who is being reformed becomes spiritual. Signified.
Those who have purified themselves by truths from the falsities of evil, and thus have been reformed by the Lord. Signified, Explained.
That those who live this faith cannot be reformed. Signified, Explained.
For all are reformed through faith united to charity.

Every man who is reformed, is reformed first as to the internal man, and afterwards as to the external. The internal man is not reformed by solely knowing and understanding truths and goods... but by willing and loving them; and the external man by speaking and doing the things which the internal man wills and loves; and, in proportion as this is done, the man is regenerated.
For the first of reformation is to live according to the precepts of the decalogue.
Man cannot be reformed except through truths from the Word...

The reason man retains (the faculty of elevating the understanding) is that he may be able to be reformed; for he is reformed through the understanding, which is effected through the Knowledges of good and truth, and through a rational view from them...
In the first state, which is called that of reformation, man is in full liberty of acting according to the Rational of his understanding; and in the second, which is the state of regeneration...
That the Divine virtue and operation, meant by the holy Spirit, are in general reformation and regeneration... General article.
The quality of man's internal unless he is reformed by the Lord. Described.
For (the will and understanding) are first to be instructed and reformed; and, through these, the two faculties of the external man, which cause him to speak and act.
On Reformation and Regeneration, Chapter.

There are two states through which man must pass, while from natural he is becoming spiritual: the first is called reformation; and the second, regeneration. In the first, man looks from his natural state towards a spiritual one, and longs for it; in the second he becomes spiritual natural. The first state is formed through truths which must be of faith, through which he looks to charity; the second is formed through the goods of charity... Or, the first state is one of thought from the understanding; and the second, of love from the will... A man who has commenced the first state, can after death be introduced into the second; but he who has not entered into the first state (here) cannot be introduced into the second after death. (These two states illustrated by comparisons.)
That the first act of the new birth is called reformation, which is of the understanding; and the second is called regeneration, which is of the will and thence of the understanding. General article.

So long as anyone sees... that evil is evil, and good good, and thinks that good ought to be chosen, the state is called reformation; but when he wills to shun evil and do good, the state of regeneration begins.

But no one can be said to be reformed through the Knowledges of Truths alone... But he is a reformed man who is in the affection of truth for the sake of truth; for this affection conjoins itself with the will; and, if it advances, it conjoins the will with the understanding, and then regeneration begins.
That the internal man is to be reformed first, and, through this, the external; and that thus man is regenerated. General article.
For the internal man is reformed through truths...
Consequently, he cannot be reformed.
The greater is the force required to reform.
A means to his reformation.
The reformation of other Spirits would be more difficult.
He acquired this reformation as it were in sleep... and it is the first reformation.
(The reformation of evil Spirits by punishments.) SE 3528:end. SE 3811. SE 3849.
He is reformed so that he can subsist in the least of his evil.
When man is in the bodily life, he can be reformed. Explained.
But in the other life... they are not reformed. Explained.
They are vastated as to the gross externals... and thus reformed...
Man cannot be reformed by taking away these Societies...
Thus nothing is wanting for man to be reformed, if he will.
The reformation of the Church. Treated of.
To create = to reform. Explained, Illustrated. AE 295.
The reformation of the gentiles. Treated of.
For man is reformed by the dissipation of evils and falsities by truths applied to life.
Reformation as to the natural man. Treated of.
The instauration anew, or reformation, of the Church. Signified.
The instauration of the Church, and the reformation of those who are of the Church. Signified. AE 730:27.
8. Thus, and no otherwise, is man reformed.
Reformation is effected in this order...
As man cannot be reformed, unless he thinks, etc. from himself...
This Reciprocal is necessary for reformation.
He is reformed by the admission of his thoughts into the Societies of Heaven.
For externals must be reformed through internals...
Man is not reformed by external means, but by internal means... Still, he is further reformed by external means, when ho has previously been reformed by internal means. Explained.
Hence everyone can be reformed; and to be reformed is nothing else than to be removed from evil loves.
Such do those become who have once been reformed, and do not remain so.
Thus it is the will which is to be reformed... AE 1171:5.
The analogy between the formation of man... and his reformation. Explained.
Those who do good from obedience are those who are reformed. LJPost 352.
